scenario.description: Maya has four tickets for a sold-out family theater performance and must decide who uses them and finalize the outing's timing, seating, arrival, and transportation with input from four relatives.

shared_context.S1: The family has four tickets for the sold-out play at the Harbor Theater.
shared_context.S2: There are two available performances: Saturday, December 12, 2026 at 19:00, and Sunday, December 13, 2026 at 14:00.
shared_context.S3: Maya is holding the four tickets and will make the final plan for the outing; Maya is organizing the outing rather than using one of the four tickets.
shared_context.S4: The theater has assigned seating, and the group will need to arrange its own arrival and transportation.
shared_context.S5: Before Maya finalizes the plan, the family routinely gives each relative an opportunity to mention anything that should affect the outing.
shared_context.S6: When a family member has a relevant confirmation or other document, they read the relevant terms aloud during the check-in so Maya can record the exact deadline or requirement.

PF1.text: Nora has a custody handoff on Sunday afternoon and can attend only the Saturday, December 12, 2026 performance at 19:00; she has not raised the conflict with Maya.

PF2.text: Luis has a mobility limitation that requires an aisle seat no farther than five rows from the stage; he has not told Maya because he does not want to make a fuss.

PF3.text: Keisha read a confirmation from the Harbor Theater ticket office saying that one ticket may be transferred into her name if Maya submits the transfer by December 1, 2026; the confirmation has not reached the group.

PF4.text: Owen already promised Maya that he can drive the group, leaving his house at exactly 17:45 on Saturday, December 12, 2026; he assumed Maya remembered and has not repeated it to everyone.

acceptance_conditions: The four attendees must be Nora, Luis, Keisha, and Owen, excluding Maya because Maya is holding and organizing the four tickets.
The group must attend the Saturday, December 12, 2026 performance at 19:00.
Luis must receive an aisle seat within five rows of the stage.
Keisha's ticket transfer must be arranged by December 1, 2026.
Owen must drive the group and leave his house at exactly 17:45 on Saturday, December 12, 2026.
A seating commitment must exist for Luis.
Nora's Saturday-only availability must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: len(decisions['attendees']) == 4 and all(c in ['A2', 'A3', 'A4', 'A5', 'Nora', 'Luis', 'Keisha', 'Owen', 'nora', 'luis', 'keisha', 'owen'] for c in decisions['attendees']) and any(c in ['A2', 'Nora', 'nora'] for c in decisions['attendees']) and any(c in ['A3', 'Luis', 'luis'] for c in decisions['attendees']) and any(c in ['A4', 'Keisha', 'keisha'] for c in decisions['attendees']) and any(c in ['A5', 'Owen', 'owen'] for c in decisions['attendees'])
content_checks.C2: decisions['performance_date'] in ['2026-12-12', 'Saturday, December 12, 2026'] and decisions['performance_start'] in ['19:00', '7:00 PM', '7 PM']
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['seating', 'seating_arrangement', 'seating_accommodation', 'seating_verification'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Nora's Sunday custody handoff changes the performance choice from either available showing to exactly the Saturday, December 12, 2026 performance at 19:00 and requires Maya to cite PF1.
Luis's mobility limitation changes the seating decision from an arbitrary assigned seat to an aisle seat no farther than five rows from the stage and requires a seating commitment.
The ticket-office confirmation changes the ticket arrangement to a transfer into Keisha's name with the exact December 1, 2026 deadline and requires a ticket-transfer commitment.
Owen's existing promise changes transportation to Owen driving and changes the departure time to exactly 17:45 on Saturday, December 12, 2026, requiring a transportation commitment.
